summary: Domain registrar and small-business web services. Carried two share classes from its 2015 IPO until Class B was retired during 2024, and presented share counts and per-share figures per class throughout, which is why its XBRL leaves the count blank for five years in the middle of that period.

annotations.shares_outstanding_end: Read from the 10-K balance-sheet parenthetical and summed across the two share classes, because companyfacts carries no share count at all for FY2019-FY2023 — no outstanding, no issued, no weighted average, in any namespace. GoDaddy presented those figures per class, so every fact is dimensional, and companyfacts publishes only the undimensioned context. Summing is verified rather than assumed: the FY2019 10-K reports its prior year as 168,549,000 Class A plus 6,254,000 Class B, and companyfacts carries FY2018 as 174,803,000 — the sum exactly. FY2024 agrees the same way at 141,208,000. Every other year is accepted only where the filing reporting it also agrees, on an overlapping column, with a year already established, so the reading spreads outward from those two anchors rather than being trusted on its own.

caveats: Summing share classes is specific to this filer and deliberately not a general rule. It is right here because GoDaddy's two classes are economically equivalent and its own filings reconcile to the sum; a filer whose classes differ in economics — Berkshire's A against its B — must be converted rather than added.

FY2023 previously showed 151,452,000, which is that year's diluted weighted-average share count standing in for a period-end figure. It is replaced here by 142,310,000, the actual count, so the row means one thing across the whole series rather than changing definition for a single year.
The FY2021 10-K's balance-sheet parenthetical does not parse, so FY2021 comes from the FY2022 filing's prior-year column instead. Both filings agree on FY2022, which is what licenses using it.
Only shares outstanding is authored here. Everything else about this filer resolves from the global tier and is left alone.
